publications.json.what_it_would_claim: Two kinases have been proposed as handles on EWSR1::NR4A3 — SGK1, which the fusion installs, and DNA-PK, which stabilises the protein the fusion carries. Verified at primary-record level, one of them is unworked ground with a clean within-section IHC control and no clinical-stage chemistry, and the other is a family-level mechanism with measured paralogue redundancy and a troubled clinical class. Publishing the distinction is worth more than publishing either lane, because the field's own state-of-the-art review still lists SGK1 as a fusion target with nothing added since 2006.
publications.json._note: ⚠ ONE ENDPOINT FOR BOTH ROUTES IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE HONEST CALL. Neither lane can carry a paper alone: SGK1's EMC evidence is ten tumours from 2006 and DNA-PK's is a negative-leaning transfer argument. What IS publishable is the pair — the observation that this disease has two named druggable kinases in its record and neither has been touched in twenty years. If the SGK1 expression read (emc-sgk1-lane-assessment.md §4c) or the 2012 gene list comes back positive, split PUB-SGK1 out and demote this to the DNA-PK half.

routes.json.display_name: DNA-PK inhibition as an indirect NR4A3 destabiliser
routes.json.title: DNA-PK inhibition as an indirect NR4A3 destabiliser
routes.json.purpose: If DNA-PK phosphorylation of NR4A3 blocks its ubiquitination, does inhibiting DNA-PK lower EWSR1::NR4A3 protein without needing any ligand for NR4A3 and without building any induced complex?

grade.value: SURVIVES AS A ROUTE, NOT AT RANK 9 — the mechanism is real and doubly replicated, and it is a PAN-NR4A family axis with measured paralogue redundancy, seen only in vascular smooth muscle on wild-type NOR1, in a drug class whose two most advanced agents have published reports of early termination for limited activity and of severe late toxicity. Its remaining value is one honest paragraph inside the DDR assessment, not a route of its own.

routes.json.rationale: NR4A3 has no orthosteric ligand and no assembled ternary complex, which is what blocks every proximity route. Regulating the protein through its OWN post-translational brake sidesteps both: DNA-PK phosphorylates NOR1 in its N-terminal domain and thereby prevents its ubiquitination, so inhibiting the kinase should lower the protein with no NR4A3 binder of any kind. The domain carrying that modification is retained intact in the commonest fusion, because NR4A3's exons 1 and 2 are non-coding and the type-1 fusion carries NR4A3(1-626) whole.

supporting_evidence.what_it_supports: DNA-PK complexes with NOR1, phosphorylates its N-terminal domain, prevents its ubiquitination, and DNA-PK inhibition lowers NOR1 protein — in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells, on wild-type endogenous NOR1
an independent second group reproduces the DNA-PKcs/NOR1 axis in human pulmonary artery smooth muscle, though attributing it to protein synthesis rather than to blocked ubiquitination
the DNA-PK/NR4A interaction is real and family-level; NR4A transcriptional activity is dispensable for it

⛔ AGAINST the route, and recorded here rather than in a caveat: PRKDC shows no EMC-specific elevation in either readable EMC series, and the two disagree on the sign. It does not test the post-translational mechanism; it removes the tumour-versus-comparator abundance argument a reader would otherwise reach for.

remaining_unknowns: Which residue DNA-PK phosphorylates. The primary paper localises it only to 'the N-terminal domain' and the residue is in its paywalled body, so no sequence-level or conservation check can be built.
Whether EWSR1::NR4A3 is ubiquitinated at all, and by which E3 — the entire degradation-brake logic is inherited from wild-type NOR1 in a non-transformed vascular cell.
Whether a DNA-PK site sitting downstream of a 431-residue EWSR1 low-complexity domain is still accessible and still coupled to the same brake.

Whether fusion abundance is set by degradation at all, given that the translocation places NR4A3 under the 5' partner's promoter and the transcriptional input is the one established thing about this system.
Whether the two primary papers' incompatible mechanisms (blocked ubiquitination vs protein synthesis) resolve in favour of the one this route needs.

required_validation.what: A western blot showing DNA-PK inhibition lowers EWSR1::NR4A3 protein in a cell carrying the fusion
Identification of the phosphorylated residue, then its conservation across NR4A1/2/3 and across all reported EMC breakpoints
Any evidence that the axis is not paralogue-redundant, which the primary literature currently states that it is

distinct_from.axis: where the degradation signal comes from
distinct_from.why: the degrader INSTALLS a degradation event with a designed molecule and can in principle tune selectivity through the ternary interface; this route RELEASES an existing brake with a kinase inhibitor and has no interface to tune — it therefore retires the degrader's two hardest blockers and imports a worse selectivity position, not a better one

distinct_from.axis: which DDR property is being used
distinct_from.why: the ATR route uses a REPLICATION-STRESS phenotype inherited from the FET-fusion class; this route uses a PROTEIN-STABILITY mechanism measured on NR4A3 itself. Both live in DDR and they are different arguments resting on different evidence, which is why the DNA-PK observation belongs inside the ATR assessment as a stated contribution rather than merged into it

routes.json.closure_note: NOT closed, and the reason to keep it open is narrow and worth stating precisely: the pan-NR4A redundancy kills the SELECTIVITY case, not the DESTABILISATION case. A route that lowers wild-type NR4A3 alongside the fusion is a bad therapeutic proposition and still a real biological observation about a disease whose driver turns out to be a substrate of a clinically drugged kinase. Nobody in twenty-five years of NR4A DNA-repair biology or thirty years of EMC biology has connected the two — measured as 73 forward citations of the two foundational papers with no EMC and no NR4A3-fusion sarcoma record among them.

publication.contribution: The negative half, and the reason the pair is worth publishing: a mechanism that looks like it removes the degrader's two hardest blockers, verified at primary level, and found to be a family-level axis with measured paralogue redundancy in a drug class with two published development setbacks. Drop it and the paper loses its counterexample.

readiness.why_not_higher: Every EMC-relevant statement this route can make is an inference from vascular smooth muscle. There is no EMC measurement, no fusion measurement and no computed result — an internal note is exactly what that supports.
missing: any measurement on a fusion protein
any measurement in a sarcoma cell
evidence_required: that EWSR1::NR4A3 protein level responds to DNA-PK inhibition
experiment_required: a DNA-PK inhibitor dose-response with NR4A3 western blot in an EMC line

timing.rationale: The decisive experiment needs a bench and the decisive literature detail needs a paywall crossed. Neither is bought by waiting, and further reasoning against vascular-smooth-muscle data produces confident-sounding conclusions about a sarcoma nobody has tested — the failure mode the register exists to prevent. What monitoring buys is cheap: the class is under active clinical development, so its safety and activity picture will keep moving whether or not this program acts.
timing.six_month_delta: Little on the biology. Possibly more on the class, which is accumulating published trial outcomes.
timing.two_year_delta: Material only if someone tests a FET fusion for the phenotype, or if NR4A3-fusion material reaches a group already working on NR4A DNA-repair biology.
timing.automation_outlook: The literature watch is fully automatable. The judgement about what a pan-family mechanism means for a selectivity-constrained program is not.

next.best_next_action: Fold the observation into emc-atr-vulnerability-assessment.md as a contributing paragraph with its limits stated inside it, and stop there. Do not build sequence-level work on a residue nobody has published.

routes.json.display_name: SGK1 — a druggable kinase the fusion installs
routes.json.title: SGK1 — a druggable kinase the fusion installs
routes.json.purpose: EWS/NOR1 induces SGK1 and 10 of 10 fusion-positive EMC tumours overexpress SGK1 protein against non-neoplastic cells in the same biopsies — is SGK1 a dependency of this disease rather than a marker of it, and can a structurally characterised AGC kinase be a handle when the driver transcription factor is not?

grade.value: SURVIVES, AND ITS CENTRAL CLAIM VERIFIES AT PRIMARY LEVEL INCLUDING THE INTERNAL CONTROL — unworked ground rather than abandoned ground, measured as 10 forward citations in 20 years with no SGK1 follow-up among them and a 2020 field review still listing it as an established fusion target with nothing added. ⛔ Two corrections to the memo's framing: no SGK1 inhibitor has ever entered a clinical trial, and the same group's 2012 human-model repeat of the screen is a paywalled gene list that could quietly close the lane.

routes.json.rationale: When the driver is an undruggable fusion transcription factor, the highest-value node is a druggable enzyme whose expression the fusion directly installs and which is absent from the normal counterpart tissue — that supplies a discrimination the driver itself cannot. SGK1 is the only such node with EMC-specific human protein data: 10 of 10 fusion-positive tumours overexpress it by IHC against non-neoplastic cells in the same biopsy sections, and it is a structurally characterised AGC kinase with a 1.9 Å catalytic-domain structure and a decade of tool chemistry.

supporting_evidence.what_it_supports: the fusion induces SGK1 in a tet-regulated rat chondrogenic line, and 10/10 fusion-positive EMC tumours overexpress SGK1 protein against a within-section non-neoplastic control and against other sarcoma types
SGK1's ATP site is structurally characterised and atypical among kinases, which is what makes ATP-competitive design tractable
an SGK1 inhibitor reduces viability in two rhabdomyosarcoma lines — evidence that the target class is tractable in a sarcoma cell, and evidence about a different sarcoma with a different driver

remaining_unknowns: Whether SGK1 is a DEPENDENCY of EMC or a marker of it. No knockdown, no inhibitor and no rescue has ever been done in an EMC cell — the 2006 paper does not claim otherwise.
Whether SGK1 reappeared when the same group repeated the screen in a human mesenchymal stem-cell model in 2012. The abstract names no gene and the list is paywalled.
Whether SGK1 is measurably high in EMC in any independent cohort. The two readable EMC series in this repository have never been read for it.
How strongly the 10/10 IHC result may be stated: the antibody, scoring threshold, reader blinding and the size of the other-sarcoma comparator are not establishable from the open record.
Whether SGK1 can be inhibited with useful margin over SGK2/SGK3 and the AKT family — an AGC-family selectivity problem that no clinical programme has yet had to solve.

required_validation.what: SGK1 expression in EMC in an independent cohort — GSE24369 (GPL6244) and GSE4303 (GPL3290), with PPARG requested alongside as a same-provenance comparator
The 2012 human-model gene list — does SGK1 appear?
SGK1 knockdown or inhibition in an EMC cell, with a viability readout

distinct_from.why: the ncBAF route is a DepMap transfer prior over 91 sarcoma lines none of which is EMC and it came back negative; SGK1 comes from EMC TUMOUR PROTEIN in ten patients and has never been tested for dependency at all. Opposite evidence shapes: one has a functional readout in the wrong disease, the other has an expression readout in the right one

distinct_from.axis: which fusion-installed node is being used
distinct_from.why: PPARG and SGK1 are the SAME GROUP'S two reported fusion targets and the 2020 field review lists them in one sentence. They are separate routes because one is a nuclear receptor with approved agonists and an open agonist-vs-redundancy direction question, and the other is a kinase with no clinical chemistry at all — the actionability arguments do not transfer between them

distinct_from.axis: which kinase, and which direction the fusion relates to it
distinct_from.why: the fusion INSTALLS SGK1, so SGK1 inhibition is aimed at something the tumour has and normal tissue does not; DNA-PK acts ON the fusion's own protein and is present everywhere. The first has a therapeutic-index argument available to it in principle and the second does not

routes.json.closure_note: Open, and unusually cheaply advanceable for a route this starved: two of its three validations are literature or public data, and only the third needs a bench.

publication.contribution: The positive half: a druggable kinase with EMC-specific human protein data and a within-section internal control, verified at primary level, measured to have been cited ten times in twenty years without a single follow-up — and the honest statement of what would have to be true for it to matter, including that nobody has tested it for dependency and that no SGK1 inhibitor has entered a clinical trial.

readiness.why_not_higher: The entire EMC evidence base is one 2006 IHC series whose Methods are unreadable, and this program has added no measurement to it yet. The expression read in section 4c of the assessment is the cheapest thing that would change that, and it has not been run.
missing: an independent EMC expression reading for SGK1
any functional test in an EMC cell
evidence_required: SGK1 elevation in an independent EMC cohort
evidence of dependency rather than expression
experiment_required: SGK1 knockdown or inhibitor dose-response in an EMC line

timing.rationale: Two of its three open questions are $0 and neither has been attempted in twenty years: a two-gene expression read against series this repository has already characterised, and a paywalled gene list that one library login settles. Nothing about waiting improves either, and the lane is currently ranked on a claim nobody had checked.
timing.six_month_delta: None from waiting. Everything available now is available now.
timing.two_year_delta: Material only through EMC model access, which eleven other routes also wait on.
timing.automation_outlook: The expression read and the citation watch are fully automatable; grading an IHC series whose Methods are unreadable is not.

at primary level **[API]** and the measurement is *cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells*, on
**wild-type endogenous NOR1**, with NOR1 **protein** level moving — but the record is
`isOpenAccess: false` with **no PMCID**, so **the site is in the paywalled body and cannot be confirmed
at $0**. **(b)** Retention holds and is read off this repository's own `OBJ-FUS-T1` /
`OBJ-NR4A3-WT` definitions — but retention of a domain is not retention of a regulation, and the site
itself is still unnamed, so no sequence-level check can be built on it. **(c)** ⚠ **DepMap cannot answer
the third**: [`fet-ddr-axis-scan.json`](../modalities/fet-ddr-axis-scan.json) records `PRKDC` under
`genes_requested_but_absent` and reports it as `null` — an **absent reading**, alongside the canonical
pan-essential `POLR2A`, which is itself a reason to distrust the column set rather than the gene.
⭐ **But a DIFFERENT PRKDC question turned out to be answerable from disk and was answered:**
[`emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json`](../modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json) already held
per-sample values for a **1,299-gene panel containing `PRKDC`** across every EMC-bearing GEO series,
and nobody had read it. **`PRKDC` shows no EMC-specific elevation and the two readable series
disagree on the sign** —
[`emc-kinase-lane-panel-read.json`](../modalities/emc-kinase-lane-panel-read.json).
⛔ **And the finding that moves the lane was not on this list at all:** PMID 21979916 (70 citations,
four years earlier) and PMID 30784586 state that the DNA-PK/NR4A axis is a **family** mechanism and
that **NR4A1 and NR4A2 are redundant** in it.

same group repeated the whole screen in a HUMAN model in 2012 (PMID 22592656) and the abstract names no

Six lanes resolve on a **single** `emc-expression-datasets.yml` dispatch against the two readable EMC
series (`GSE24369`/GPL6244, 6 EMC vs 29 comparators, 93.2% probe mapping; `GSE4303`/GPL3290, 10 EMC,
58.2% after UniGene rescue) — both already characterised in
map_edits_required.why: ⛔ TWO MEASURED CORRECTIONS, both read from the characterisation artifact this sentence already cites. (a) '29 comparators' does not belong to GSE24369. That series has 42 samples — 6 EMC, 17 low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma, 6 desmoid fibromatosis, 6 myxofibrosarcoma, 5 solitary fibrous tumour and 2 pooled skeletal-muscle RNA — so the comparator arm is 36. `29` is the sample count of a DIFFERENT series, GSE80126, recorded three entries away in the same artifact ('returned by the EMC/NR4A3 GEO DataSets query (29 samples, 2016/10/20)'). A neighbouring number was picked up. (b) 93.2% and 58.2% are `accession_resolution_rate`, NOT probe mapping — on GSE24369, 20,324 of 28,459 probes map, which is 71.4%. Calling an accession-resolution rate 'probe mapping' inflates by ~22 points the fraction of the array a reader thinks is usable. Evidence for both: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json → /part_b/platforms/GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz (per-sample titles; accession_resolution_rate 0.932; n_mapped 20324; n_probes 28459) and .../GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz (16 samples; accession_resolution_rate 0.582). Reproduced by research/modalities/emc_kinase_lane_panel_read.py.
